`uuid` is a MitID specific claim.

question: Hi! We’re integrating Finnish, Norwegian and Swedish BankID-s to verify the customer’s name and date of birth. We get the date of birth from Finnish and Norwegian but not Swedish BankID. We get only the SSN from Swedish BankID. Can we assume that the first 6 or 8 digits of the SSN correspond to the date of birth? Can it be 6 digits or is it always 8 digits? <[link]>
answer:
Hi a user,

The SSN is provided by BankID itself and we do not modify or control it.

As such we cannot make garantuees to what the format will be.

We would suggest that you make a defensive parser that checks the amount numbers, and only assumes that the first 8 digits are the birthdate, if there are 12 digits in total.

If there are 10 digits, then the you can likely assume that the year starts with 19.

answer:
Hi a user,
You can retrieve (and view) the signed PDFs after all signatories have signed the signature order. After the signature order is closed, we delete all PDFs from our servers (unless you configure document retention): <https://docs.criipto.com/signatures/graphql/examples/#closing-a-signature-order>
So it's up to you to implement the storage mechanism for the documents signed via your application.

question:
Hi,
Currently, we are using MitId with Criipto by directing a WebView in our Expo React Native app to our .NET6 backend, that serves the Criipto MitID page. This means that all the authentication happens on the backend server, and it can verify the user, generate tokens and send it to the app. However, as I understand it, this is not the recommended way to handle MitID login. It is also causing us problems, as it is giving us QR codes, that our users obviously can't scan, as they are shown on the same device as they would scan it with..

So, I want to switch out our solution with the recommended way. However, I'm having a bit of trouble understanding how it works. As I said, we have:
1. .NET6 Backend server
2. Expo React Native app
Looking at your documentation for Expo integration, I would initiate the login in the app and receive the JWT. How do I go about sending this to the backend server? It doesn't know about the JWT and thus can't verify it. Do I make a separate integration on the Backend server that can call Criipto to verify the JWT? Or what do I do from there?
answer:
>  Currently, we are using MitId with Criipto by directing a WebView
MitID does, per its terms, not allow WebViews, this is also described in our documentation - it's a pain, but it is a requirement that a full browser view that shows the address bar is used.

Hello! We are leveraging the swedish BankID native signatures to integrate best in our flow. Loving the overall flow so far, as well as everything on the styling front we can do.

We do have a couple of issues that we are running in to, which aren’t specified in detail in the docs:

1. What is the best endpoint to use for leveraging native signatures? Is that /text/sign? Or are there other means inside Criipto Verify?
2. BankID allows you (similar to a message on login) to format the signtext using markdown. It appears this does not work, or I’m doing something wrong. How can we best approach this?
3. We’d like to allow the user to choose their way of signing (app or QR) on the criipto page. How can we best configure this? Ideally we would just send configure the allowed signing option in our application, but that appears to result in the user being redirected to a login flow in the app.
Example encoded markdown I provided (it’s an online example taken from the BankID docs):
``````
answer:
Hi a user 

1: That is the only endpoint where we expose native signatures, so yes, /sign/text is the best :)

2: You must send it via `login_hint=message:BASE64MARKDOWN`

3: We do not support method-selection for native signatures, I’m afraid - only for authentication. You will have to host the relevant buttons in your website/app

question:
Hi,
I am trying to figure out the best architecture for enabling Criipto Verify in my application, but due to my (in)experience in the area, any help to point me in the right direction would be very much appreciated. :-)

*About the application:* The app stores data about customers, and is built using Angular and AWS Amplify, AppSync and Cognito User Pools. App users (employees) creates data about customers in the app, and they access the app and data by logging in with their Cognito users. I do not want to use Criipto Verify for the App users.

*Why I need to use Criipto:* I want to create a second application/interface, where customers can access their data, and I want to use Criipto Verify as the authorization layer. Seems easy to me (just authorize, and use the token to query AppSync) -- but when I am trying to figure out _how_ this architecture should look like, I get completely lost.

I have tried to set up OIDC authorization rules in AppSync where valid tokens are granted access to data (token ssn == data ssn) and it works well when querying AppSync manually from Postman. However, when querying AppSync with Amplify libs I get an error about no logged in user. Which is correct, because I have not integrated Cognito and Criipto. If I set up an integration, the customer must first log in with their Cognito credentials I believe, and I want a very simple solution where each customer can access their data by using their SE BankID only. No registration, nothing. And most important -- any customer should never ever be able to authenticate in the app for employees.

What are the pro's / con's with these two different solutions?
How should I implement Criipto Verify given my application architecture and needs?

Any guidance, or best practices for Amplify/Angular, would be very much appreciated. Thanks!
answer:
Hi a user

Interesting usecase!
I'm afraid we don't have any experience with AWS Amplify.

However it should be possible to setup Criipto Verify directly in AWS Cognito: <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/integrations/aws-cognito/> maybe that will meet your needs?

You might want two user pools, one for employees and one for customers, and then configure AWS Amplify based on the context?

1. Is it possible to obtain the personal number (socialno) upon closing the document (when the user has signed the document)? If so, I suspect I need to configure a document when creating it?
2. How to correctly remove all login options when creating a signature document and only keep BankID NO?
answer:
Hi Abyl!

1. Yes, you can extract the JWT evidence from the document signature when you close the document: <https://docs.criipto.com/signatures/graphql/examples/#include-signature-information>
2. You can either select the specific eID you want via the dashboard, or configure it directly on the signature order: <https://docs.criipto.com/signatures/graphql/examples/#changing-authentication-options>

question:
Hi support, i have a question regarding the callback after login with mitid.
When i have logged in, i would like to be redirected to the page the person came from forexample
<[link]>

how would i write this in the "add callback urls" under edit application ? Seems i can only write static paths forexample <[link]>

It is possible i just redirect that page to the correct page using the state to add id's but i would rather it just came straight back?
answer:
We do not support wildcard redirect URIs, you have to define the full URL including the path - however the query segment is optional.

So you could use an additional query param (or the `state` ) param to carry your internal redirect state.

That is also how this problem is generally solved.

question:
Hello.
I need help with a step or 2 in our test implementation.
We have a website and an API and are trying to use the <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/getting-started/oidc-intro/#authenticate-with-back-channel-authorization-code-flow|The Authorization Code Flow>.
Currently as I understand it this is our approach:
1. Website requests a criipto link from our API. Our API builds a link like the one below (this link seems to work fine when inserted into a browser).
2. Website redirects user to this link, and MitID auth flow initiates.
3. After authentication, the callback happens as a Http GET request in the browser.
Question A) Can the callback happen from the criipto server to the API instead? Or does the user's browser HAVE to redirect to the website (who then has to pass the "code" parameter to our api)?
Question B) If instead of a website, we want to use this from our App, we can't just send the below Link to our app can we? Where in your docs does it describe this case?
Question C) I may have multiple questions regarding app, because if the flows happens in the app, who handles the callback/redirect?

[link]<[link]> message:QXV0b3Jpc2VyIGRpZyBzZWx2IG92ZXIgZm9yIFNheG8uY29t
answer:
Hi Nikolaj,
I can point you in the right direction, but we may need support if you have more specific questions about app integration :slightly_smiling_face:
A) The browser must redirect to the `redirect_uri`. The redirect provides the code, which your website then forwards to your API for token exchange. (We highly recommend using an OIDC library or <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/integrations/|one of our integrations> to handle token exchange etc.)
B) Apps require custom/deep links as the `redirect_uri`, see <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/guides/appswitch/|App switching> docs for app integration. And remember, for apps you should use the PKCE flow (see <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/getting-started/best-security-practices/#authorization-code-flow|OIDC best practices>.)

question:
Hey!

I'm implementing Controlled Transfer for MitId in our app. Due to the nature of our app, we can't guarantee a time between the MitId login and the transfer to our service provider. Does the `transferTokenExchangeCode` have an expiration time?
answer:
Yes, you should store the `mitid:ct:sid`  and only use it to obtain a `transferTokenExchangeCode` once you need to actually do a Controlled Transfer.
The `mitid:ct:sid` will remain valid until the original MitID token expires. We cannot guarantee a specific lifetime since the tokens originate from the MitID core system, but currently the tokens expire around 5 hours after the initial MitID login. In the near future, we will add an additional claim to the JWT you receive from us to indicate when the `mitid:ct:sid` expires.
We cannot guarantee any specific lifetime for the `transferTokenExchangeCode` since it originates from the MitID core system.

Peter
answer:
Hi Peter,
If you need customers to sign for a company (as a "company signatory"/"tegningsberettiget medarbejder"), the CPR number is necessary to look up users with Erhvervsstyrelsen. There is some complication behind the scenes here, since company signatories can either exist in MitID Erhverv (which does not need CPR) or in Erhvervsstyrelsen. For company signatories, we will thus always ask the user for their CPR, even if we do not forward it to you in the JWT.
Hope this helps - I will update our documentation to make this more clear.

question:
MitID: To prevent circumvention of a system, I'm considering storing `cprNumberIdentifier` to ensure users don't create multiple accounts. But I'd of course rather not store (hashed) CPR at all, and would prefer to rely on `sub` instead. But in what situations can I expect a users `sub` to change, and how often? Are we talking very few edge cases, generally? Or only if a user gets a new MitID?

Or does it change even if the user changes their MitID username?

Perhaps it's better to store the MitID `uuid`  instead? More persistent than `sub` but less sensitive than CPR?
answer:
a user The `uuid` and `sub` are equivalent considered from a lifetime-perspective (we derive the `sub` from the `uuid`, but the `sub` is tenant-specific, while the `uuid` is end-user-specific).

All 3 can change. CPR number changes are probably the most prevalent one, but no official statistics exist.

We have a website that uses Criipto to signin with MitID using nextauth.
Now we are making an app that wraps the website in a webview.

For the app I want to persist the login session behind faceID, so they don't have to login again, for say 30days.

answer:
_Firstly:_
MitID can, generally speaking, NOT be wrapped in a webview.
A requirement is that the user can always see the URL bar, and generally recommends use of Custom Chrome Tabs + ASWebAuthenticationSession.

>  For the app I want to persist the login session behind faceID, so they don't have to login again, for say 30days.
For this case you will probably want our upcoming support for DPoP based refresh tokens. It is not ready yet, but this will let you try a biometrics/passkey protected device private key to a token used to refresh Criipto id_tokens

question:

2. I assume `signatory_status` can be one of `SIGNED`, `REJECTED` and `ERROR`? Or are there other possible values?

4. Is it possible to redirect back to this URL if the user cancels the signing? E.g.  `signatory_status=CANCELLED`
answer:
1. Not correctly, no, those two params should provide you with the baseline for querying additional information. As with webhook events we aim for systems to query the information they require via the GraphQL interface :slightly_smiling_face: 
2. The `signatory_status` can in theory be one of the status that is part defined by the `Signatory.SignatoryStatus` in the GraphQL schema.
3. Am a bit unsure, support can likely answer.
4. Can you elaborate on "cancel"? A user can either reject or sign on our frontend

Yes, this is expected for the Finnish tokens. A few months ago, the Finnish Trust Network provider decided that they no longer wish to return a "display name", so instead they just return a sub in the `name` claim.
We recommend that you instead parse the `given_name` and `family_name` claims and render them in whatever combination you need.

Our Criipto Verify domain keys are about to expire in 30 days. Should we have to prepare a new key on the 29th day  or will it renew automatically ?

There is no automatic renewal.
You should prepare in advance so that any metadata (JWKS) cache is refreshed when you activate the new key.

I would suggest preparing a new key within the next 14 days and then activating it within the next 30 days.

question:
Hey Support, we're addressing changes in our integration with Criipto in regards to the new <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/e-ids/finnish-trust-network/#technical-guides|FTN requirements>
and we've encountered an issue that could be worked around but we'd rather not:

1. According to the <[link] spec>, the `response_type` must be present in the Authorization request
    a. t_he request is a valid OAuth 2.0 Authorization Request, values for the *response_type and client_id parameters MUST be included* using the OAuth 2.0 request syntax, since they are REQUIRED by OAuth 2.0. The values for these parameters MUST match those in the Request Object, if present._
2. We use `response_type=code` in the authorization URL and a `"response_type": "code"` (actual value from the decoded JWT) in the request object JWT
3. Unfortunately we get a `"'response_type' parameter must match signed 'response_type' parameter"` error from your end
4. If we remove this query parameter from the URL all goes well
We don't have issues with other integrations that also use a request object, could you check on your end how this mismatch is happening? Thanks!

question:
Hi, we are currently implementing norwegian bankid login on our website, and need some guidance regarding consent to get ssn/nnin. I see there is already some discussion regarding the deprecated "bankid consent service". According to your and bankid's docs the way to not use this deprecated service is to use the nnin_altsub scope ("SSN consent - Always granted"-setting in criipto).

In the docs it states that we then must obtain consent from the user prior to the authentication flow. Do you or bankid have more details on exactly what's required when obtaining consent?

I also see at least one of our competitors are getting my ssn from bankid without obtaining my consent for the exact same usecase. Are there exemptions to the consent requirement or are some companies not following the guidelines? :thinking_face:
answer:
Hi a user
We have previously asked BankID about this. There are no specific requirements. Their answer is that you need to:
1. Have an agreement to use NNIN (i.e. legal basis in the application for BankID).
2. Follow standard GDPR policies to get user consent for using and storing personal data.
So in practice, as long as NNIN is covered in the general end user agreement regarding personal data - it should be fine. Note that it is your responsibility as a merchant to follow applicable legislation such as GDPR in this case.

question:
Hej - vores udvikler prøver at implementere jeres React standard bibliotek (<[link] - criipto/criipto-verify-react: Accept MitID, NemID, Swedish BankID, Norwegian BankID and more logins in your React app with @criipto/verify-react.>) - og er i stand til at sende brugerne over til Criipto for validering, men løber ind i et issue, når der kommer svar tilbage fra Criipto. Muligvis pga. at de bruger noget der hedder Capacitor og ikke ren React, som jeres library vist er skrevet til? Kan I evt. vurdere om der er noget de kan gøre anderledes? Eller måske er der en bug i jeres library? Eller også er det bare en inkompatibilitet med Capacitor? Eller noget fjerde :)

Udvikleren skriver: "når vi så lander retur i appen med en code som biblioteket skal "gribe" og fortsætte sin session med er det som om at uanset hvad jeg prøver på nægter biblioteket at fortsætte signeringen og lave det om til et resultat med et token. så jeg lander lidt på det stadie. at vi er vendt tilbage med en kode og så ikke kommer videre i forløbet hvilket jo ikke er hensigtsmæssigt.

jeg griber koden i en capacitor eventlistener
App.addListener('appUrlOpen', (event: URLOpenListenerEvent) => {}
<[link]>
så jeg ved at vi er kommet korrekt tilbage til appen, men her ser det så desværre ud til at biblioteket fra criipto ikke helt forstår at vi er tilbage :confused:
Når jeg tester i web fungerer alt som forventet, det er kun på native den er mystisk
Jeg benytter loginhint med appswitch og har resumeUrl til korrekt url (som nævnt har jeg testet og vi kommer tilbage til appen som forventet)"
answer:
Hej Allan

Har du mulighed for at stille mig direkte igennem til jeres udvikler :slightly_smiling_face: (<[link]> har et link til at joine slack).

Vores react pakke forventer at den kan få adgang til redirect URL fra browseren. Så på web fungerer det, da browseren bliver omstillet til <[link]>, og så hiver jo code ud fra det.

question:
Hey folks, questions about age verification:

1. At <https://docs.criipto.com/verify/guides/age-verification/> it says in the Auditing section that `id_token` is issued in an opaque way so that we can present it to criipto and then get an audit trail for the verification. However the same page also says that `id_token` response type is deprecated and that we should use `code` instead as that is the recommended approach. When doing so, the data I get back in the claim looks like this:
```{
  "country" : "DK",
  "auditId" : "alu_2c784157-f359-45f5-91b9-aff9c4908f9c",
  "is_over_18" : true
}```
      Is the `audit_id` the id I can submit to Criipto for the audit trail?
2. This `audit_id` property is also present if I use SE / BankID for verification, but from email conversations I am told that this is not an audit trail, is this the case? What is the `audit_id` then?
3. There are currently 4 age verification scopes I can supply, `is_over_15`, `is_over_16`, `is_over_18` and `is_over_21`. I'm in the situation that I actually want to verify that the age is over `20` (minimum legal age for buying wine in Sweden). Is there a way to check for that age? Or arbitrary ages (in case the laws change before you can add new scopes)?
answer:
It is correct that `response_type=id_token` is deprecated, however an `id_token` is also returned when you use code flow.

>  This `audit_id` property is also present if I use SE / BankID for verification
Hmm, it should not be.

>  I'm in the situation that I actually want to verify that the age is over `20` (minimum legal age for buying wine in Sweden)
We can add the scope - Can you share/link some relevant legal information - Would be good for our internal docs.
Arbitrary ages is not allowed as it would make it possible to determine an exact age in all instances, which would be worse for privacy.

question:
Hi, Idura! Probably a question for BankID Norge, but I'm trying my luck here anyways, as you might have the answers :slightly_smiling_face:

We are planning to use BankID Biometrics (`no:bankid:substantial`) to obtain both SSN and phone number. By using SSN Consent "Already granted" and scope `openid ssn` , we are able to obtain the users SSN without any explicit consents during the authentication flow. Which fits our use case well, apart form the missing phone number.

If we then append the scope `phone` the user will, as stated over at <[link]>, be prompted for consent. The current UX issue I'm facing is that the user is presented with the following screen (screenshot attached). No where does it indicate that continuing this process and filling out the form would be required, and the user might as well decide to skip it. If a user do decide to skip it, it would result in an OAuth error stating that the user did not consent to sharing their SSN. And the reason would be hard to understand since they did not even reach the consent form. Those who do continue and fill out the contact information form, also get the possibility to withhold consent for sharing SSN, which would result in the same OAuth error (but it is somewhat easier to understand why).

I have only tested this in the preprod (Idura test environment), so I do not yet know if it behaves the same in production. But, is this the only way of obtaining the phone number of a user — using NO BankID's form auto-filling feature?
answer: Email/phone/address flows via BankID are deprecated and will be removed end of year.

You can extract information on the signature by querying the signature information (<https://docs.idura.app/signatures/graphql/examples/#include-signature-information>).

question:
Hi Idura,

We have a WordPress website using the miniOrange plugin for MitID login. For our solution, we need to retrieve the user's CVR number upon login. Based on our research here on Slack, we understand that logging in with a private MitID is not sufficient if we need the CVR number included in the response.

We have already set up a test organization and a test employee. We successfully got the login working with a private MitID, but as mentioned, this doesn't meet our requirements. We are now trying to set it up so the user must use the MitID app for business, but we are struggling to get it activated for our test user.

Do you have a guide on how to correctly set up a test user for MitID for Business? We need this to verify that our solution can successfully fetch the CVR number associated with the user.
answer:
a user CVR numbers only apply in MitID for Business. There is no dedicated app for this, though. It boils down to the context in which it is being used.

Organizations may choose to allow their employees to use their private MitID for the authentication part, or they may choose to require them to have a employee MitID identity.
I don't think that many orgs require the latter, though, as it breaks the biometrics feature in the MitID app.

When you have completed setting up the MitID Business parts (as described in our docs), you must request a MitID Business login from us (as described here <https://docs.idura.app/verify/e-ids/danish-mitid-erhverv/> )

Hope this helps - otherwise, let me know!

question:
Hi,
I am a developer working on a web-based application. I have successfully and securely integrated the Idura API into our system.
My client is based in Norway and now wants to proceed with purchasing the *Live API* to move forward. However, we have a concern regarding the website launch.
Currently, we do *not* want to make the application publicly available because our main domain already has active users and traffic.
I have a few questions regarding the Live API approval process:
1. Is it mandatory to have a publicly accessible live website in order to get approval for the Live API?
2. If a live website is required, can we deploy the application on a *subdomain* (for example, `<[link]>`, where the main domain is `<[link]>`) for approval and testing purposes?
After approval, can we then move the application to the main domain, or does the Live API require the application to remain on the same domain used during approval?
3. Could you please share any *specific requirements or prerequisites* needed to obtain approval for the Live API?
Looking forward to your guidance.
answer:
Hi a user I assume that you are asking specifically about the Norwegian BankID on behalf of your client?
1 - If thats the case, then no it’s not mandatory to have a publicly accessible live website to set up the order.
The domain that is needed for the application is the Idura Production Domain which is configured on your tenant when going into production. That specific domain must be whitelisted as part of the application with STØ. So if you wish to integrate towards Idura with a few different domains on your end, that should be possible.

3 - The prerequisites for ordering Norwegian BankID is that the company applying must be registered as a Norwegian Company at <[link]> and they *must* have a Norwegian Bank Account.
As it’s the banks that approve the applications, this is mandatory.

question:
Hello Idura,
Recently there was pen-test on our app and we found out that the bankid implementation has this potential <[link]>. After reading the documentation I do not see a way that we as end customer we can fix it and I understand we have to contact support for this. Is it ok to do via slack or email?
Thanks
answer:
Hi a user thanks for reaching out about this.

We are aware of the problem, but at least one of the suggested mitigation(s) in the article would no longer be very effective - since iOS decided to obfuscate the IP address of browsers, the RP (or Idura) can no longer expect to do matching based on the IP addresses of the browser and BankID app, respectively.

Regarding certificate policies: Restricting these would break some user flows, as I understand it. Users that still rely on file-based BankID (so, not having a mobile app) would not be able to login if the another-device restriction were applied. So we are in a bit of a bind here, as the ToS from Finansiell Teknik explicitly disallow discriminating users.

Fixing the open redirection bug would fall squarely with Finansiell Teknik. We have suggested this to them, but have not had any luck with it so far. If you believe you have more leverage than us (which you may very well have), please try to motivate them to allow for registering a positive-list of redirect URLs :slightly_smiling_face:
